```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
# readxl is only needed if you point path_v1 / path_v2 at .xlsx files

# ---- Config -----------------------------------------------------------------

path_v1 <- "data_validation_reviewer_1.csv"   # reviewer 1, first sheet
path_v2 <- "data_validation_reviewer_2.csv"   # reviewer 2, first sheet

label_v1 <- "reviewer 1"
label_v2 <- "reviewer 2"

id_col <- "key"                        # study identifier present in both files

# Bibliographic / Rayyan-imported fields, not extracted variables.
# Move a name out of here to include it in the agreement table.
not_extraction <- c(
  "row_id", "key", "person", "title", "source", "year", "journal",
  "authors", "author_first", "abstract", "doi", "keywords", "notes",
  "notes_1", "key_findings"
)

# Cells holding a comma-separated set, so order is ignored when comparing.
multi_value_vars <- c(
  "area", "sex", "study_context", "environmental_context",
  "sport_specific_skill", "collective_behaviour",
  "asessment_technology", "assessment_method"
)

# Both files use the same 37 columns, so nothing needs remapping. If a variable
# is ever renamed or split between files, add a row here:
#   label = name to report, col_v1 = its name in file 1, col_v2 = in file 2
var_map <- data.frame(
  label = character(0), col_v1 = character(0), col_v2 = character(0),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Labels used in the results paragraph. Anything not listed here falls back to
# the column name with underscores replaced by spaces.
pretty_labels <- c(
  asessment_technology   = "assessment technology",
  assessment_described   = "assessment description",
  female_n               = "number of female participants",
  sport_specific_info    = "sport-specific information",
  sport_specific_skill   = "sport-specific skill",
  sample_size            = "sample size",
  outcome_measure        = "outcome measure",
  assessment_sample_size = "assessment sample size",
  study_design           = "study design",
  study_context          = "study context",
  assessment_timeframe   = "assessment timeframe",
  assessment_method      = "assessment method",
  environmental_context  = "environmental context",
  underpinning_theory    = "underpinning theory",
  collective_behaviour   = "collective behaviour"
)

# TRUE adds the AC1 in brackets after each percentage in the paragraph
include_ac1_in_paragraph <- FALSE

# TRUE appends a closing sentence naming the free-text fields
flag_free_text_in_paragraph <- TRUE

paragraph_docx <- "agreement_paragraph.docx"

ignore_case    <- TRUE
missing_tokens <- c("", "na", "n/a", "none", "-", "--", ".")
conf_level     <- 0.95

# Prose fields. Two extractors writing the same thing in their own words will
# almost never produce an identical string, so exact-match agreement is not a
# meaningful reliability estimate for these. They are still computed, but are
# flagged with an asterisk in the table.
# sample_size is borderline ("45 athletes" vs "45 (4 teams)") - move it here if
# you would rather treat it as free text.
free_text_vars <- c(
  "aim", "procedure", "sport_specific_info", "outcome_measure",
  "assessment_sample_size", "assessment_described"
)

# Optional regex fix-ups applied to every cell before comparison, given as
# c(pattern = replacement) and applied after lower-casing. Empty by default:
# anything added here changes the reported agreement, so add sparingly and
# report what was applied. The two below are the common cosmetic mismatches
# in these files, commented out so the default result is the unadjusted one.
value_fixups <- c(
  # "^n *= *"   = "",       # "n = 12" and "12"
  # "skills\\b" = "skill"   # "sport specific skills" and "sport specific skill"
)

# ---- Read -------------------------------------------------------------------

# Names are cleaned here rather than with janitor::clean_names(). janitor
# de-duplicates the two "notes" columns using their column *position*, which
# differs between the two workbooks (32 vs 36 columns), so a name like notes_37
# exists in neither file. make.unique() gives the same name in both.
clean_nms <- function(x) {
  x <- tolower(trimws(x))
  x <- gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "_", x)
  x <- gsub("^_+|_+$", "", x)
  make.unique(x, sep = "_")
}

read_extraction <- function(path) {
  # Everything is read as text so that a numeric 20 and a typed "20" do not
  # disagree on type alone. Takes .csv or .xlsx (first sheet).
  if (grepl("\\.csv$", path, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    d <- utils::read.csv(path, colClasses = "character", check.names = FALSE,
                         stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = character(0))
  } else {
    d <- readxl::read_xlsx(path, sheet = 1, col_types = "text")
  }
  names(d) <- clean_nms(names(d))
  as.data.frame(d, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

v1 <- read_extraction(path_v1)
v2 <- read_extraction(path_v2)

stopifnot(id_col %in% names(v1), id_col %in% names(v2))

# ---- Normalise cell values --------------------------------------------------

squish <- function(x) gsub("[[:space:]]+", " ", trimws(x))

canonicalise <- function(x, multi = FALSE) {
  x <- squish(as.character(x))
  if (ignore_case) x <- tolower(x)
  for (p in names(value_fixups)) x <- squish(gsub(p, value_fixups[[p]], x))
  x[x %in% missing_tokens] <- NA_character_

  # 20, 20.0 and " 20 " should not count as a disagreement
  num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
  is_num <- !is.na(num)
  x[is_num] <- as.character(num[is_num])

  if (multi) {
    x <- vapply(x, function(cell) {
      if (is.na(cell)) return(NA_character_)
      parts <- squish(strsplit(cell, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
      parts <- parts[nzchar(parts)]
      if (!length(parts)) return(NA_character_)
      paste(sort(unique(parts)), collapse = ", ")
    }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  }
  x
}

# ---- Gwet's AC1 -------------------------------------------------------------
# Two raters, one rating each per subject. Gwet KL (2008) Br J Math Stat
# Psychol 61:29-48.
#   pa   = observed agreement
#   pi_k = (times rater 1 used category k + times rater 2 used k) / 2n
#   pe   = sum_k pi_k (1 - pi_k) / (q - 1)
#   AC1  = (pa - pe) / (1 - pe)
# SE is Gwet's linearisation estimator; the CI uses t with n - 1 df.
#
# Written out rather than called from irrCAC so the document renders with no
# extra package and so the blank-handling is explicit. To cross-check a
# variable against the package:  irrCAC::gwet.ac1.raw(cbind(a, b))$est

gwet_ac1 <- function(x, y, conf_level = 0.95) {
  out <- list(n = 0L, q = NA_integer_, pa = NA_real_, pe = NA_real_,
              ac1 = NA_real_, se = NA_real_, lcl = NA_real_, ucl = NA_real_)
  keep <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(y)
  x <- as.character(x)[keep]
  y <- as.character(y)[keep]
  n <- length(x)
  if (n == 0L) return(out)

  cats <- sort(unique(c(x, y)))
  q <- length(cats)
  out$n <- n
  out$q <- q

  pa_i <- as.numeric(x == y)
  pa <- mean(pa_i)
  out$pa <- pa

  # only one category in play: chance agreement is undefined, AC1 is 1
  if (q == 1L) {
    out$pe <- 0
    out$ac1 <- 1
    return(out)
  }

  # pi_ik = proportion of the two raters placing study i in category k
  pi_ik <- matrix(0, nrow = n, ncol = q, dimnames = list(NULL, cats))
  ix <- cbind(seq_len(n), match(x, cats))
  iy <- cbind(seq_len(n), match(y, cats))
  pi_ik[ix] <- pi_ik[ix] + 0.5
  pi_ik[iy] <- pi_ik[iy] + 0.5

  pi_k <- colMeans(pi_ik)
  pe <- sum(pi_k * (1 - pi_k)) / (q - 1)
  ac1 <- (pa - pe) / (1 - pe)
  out$pe <- pe
  out$ac1 <- ac1

  if (n > 1L) {
    pe_i <- (sum(pi_k) - as.vector(pi_ik %*% pi_k)) / (q - 1)
    infl <- ((pa_i - pa) - 2 * (1 - ac1) * (pe_i - pe)) / (1 - pe)
    se <- sqrt(sum(infl^2) / (n * (n - 1)))
    tcrit <- stats::qt(1 - (1 - conf_level) / 2, df = n - 1)
    out$se <- se
    out$lcl <- max(-1, ac1 - tcrit * se)
    out$ucl <- min(1, ac1 + tcrit * se)
  }
  out
}

# ---- Match the two files study by study -------------------------------------

ids     <- intersect(v1[[id_col]], v2[[id_col]])
only_v1 <- setdiff(v1[[id_col]], v2[[id_col]])
only_v2 <- setdiff(v2[[id_col]], v1[[id_col]])

v1m <- v1[match(ids, v1[[id_col]]), , drop = FALSE]
v2m <- v2[match(ids, v2[[id_col]]), , drop = FALSE]

# ---- Variables to compare ---------------------------------------------------

shared <- setdiff(intersect(names(v1), names(v2)), not_extraction)
spec <- rbind(
  data.frame(label = shared, col_v1 = shared, col_v2 = shared,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  var_map
)

# ---- Compare ----------------------------------------------------------------

compare_one <- function(label, col_v1, col_v2) {
  multi <- label %in% multi_value_vars
  a <- canonicalise(v1m[[col_v1]], multi)
  b <- canonicalise(v2m[[col_v2]], multi)

  both_obs <- !is.na(a) & !is.na(b)

  # complete pairs only: both extractors recorded something
  obs <- gwet_ac1(a, b, conf_level)

  # blanks kept as a category of their own, so blank vs blank is agreement
  blk <- gwet_ac1(ifelse(is.na(a), "<blank>", a),
                  ifelse(is.na(b), "<blank>", b), conf_level)

  d <- which(both_obs & a != b)

  list(
    summary = data.frame(
      variable         = label,
      n_double         = sum(both_obs),
      n_one_blank      = sum(xor(is.na(a), is.na(b))),
      n_both_blank     = sum(is.na(a) & is.na(b)),
      pct_agree        = 100 * obs$pa,
      ac1              = obs$ac1,
      ac1_lcl          = obs$lcl,
      ac1_ucl          = obs$ucl,
      pct_agree_blanks = 100 * blk$pa,
      ac1_blanks       = blk$ac1,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ),
    disagreements = if (length(d)) data.frame(
      variable   = label,
      key        = ids[d],
      reviewer_1 = v1m[[col_v1]][d],
      reviewer_2 = v2m[[col_v2]][d],
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ) else NULL
  )
}

results <- Map(compare_one, spec$label, spec$col_v1, spec$col_v2)

agreement <- do.call(rbind, lapply(results, `[[`, "summary"))
agreement <- agreement[order(-agreement$pct_agree, agreement$variable), ]
rownames(agreement) <- NULL

disagreements <- do.call(rbind, lapply(results, `[[`, "disagreements"))
if (is.null(disagreements)) {
  disagreements <- data.frame(
    variable = character(0), key = character(0),
    reviewer_1 = character(0), reviewer_2 = character(0),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}
rownames(disagreements) <- NULL

fmt <- function(x, d = 2) ifelse(is.na(x), "-", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d))
pct <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "-", paste0(round(x), "%"))

write.csv(agreement, "agreement_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(disagreements, "agreement_disagreements.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# ---- Results paragraph ------------------------------------------------------

label_for <- function(x) {
  out <- unname(pretty_labels[x])
  ifelse(is.na(out), gsub("_", " ", x), out)
}

items <- paste0(
  label_for(agreement$variable), " ", round(agreement$pct_agree), "%",
  if (include_ac1_in_paragraph) paste0(" (AC1 ", fmt(agreement$ac1), ")") else ""
)

para <- paste0(
  "Data extraction agreement between the two reviewers was assessed across ",
  nrow(agreement), " variables for ", length(ids),
  " studies. Raw agreement was as follows: ",
  paste(items, collapse = ", "), "."
)

if (flag_free_text_in_paragraph) {
  ft <- label_for(intersect(agreement$variable, free_text_vars))
  if (length(ft)) {
    ft_list <- if (length(ft) > 1) {
      paste0(paste(ft[-length(ft)], collapse = ", "), " and ", ft[length(ft)])
    } else ft
    para <- paste0(
      para, " Agreement for ", ft_list,
      " reflects exact matching of free-text responses and therefore",
      " understates the extent to which the reviewers agreed in substance."
    )
  }
}

# Export to Word. officer if it is installed, otherwise pandoc via rmarkdown.
# The plain-text version is always written, so nothing is lost either way.
writeLines(para, sub("\\.docx$", ".md", paragraph_docx))
docx_written <- FALSE

if (requireNamespace("officer", quietly = TRUE)) {
  officer::read_docx() |>
    officer::body_add_par("Data extraction agreement", style = "heading 1") |>
    officer::body_add_par(para, style = "Normal") |>
    print(target = paragraph_docx)
  docx_written <- TRUE
} else if (requireNamespace("rmarkdown", quietly = TRUE) &&
           rmarkdown::pandoc_available()) {
  rmarkdown::pandoc_convert(
    input  = normalizePath(sub("\\.docx$", ".md", paragraph_docx)),
    to     = "docx",
    output = paragraph_docx
  )
  docx_written <- TRUE
}
```

# Data extraction agreement

```{r agreement-table, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

tab <- data.frame(
  Variable        = ifelse(agreement$variable %in% free_text_vars,
                           paste0(agreement$variable, "*"),
                           agreement$variable),
  n               = agreement$n_double,
  `Raw agreement` = pct(agreement$pct_agree),
  `Gwet's AC1`    = fmt(agreement$ac1),
  `95% CI`        = ifelse(is.na(agreement$ac1_lcl), "-",
                           paste0(fmt(agreement$ac1_lcl), " to ",
                                  fmt(agreement$ac1_ucl))),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

kable(tab, align = "lrrrr", row.names = FALSE) |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, latex_options = "hold_position")

```

\* Free-text field. Two reviewers describing the same study in their own words
will rarely produce an identical string, so exact-match agreement understates
reliability for these variables.

# Results paragraph

Text below is written to `r paragraph_docx` for pasting into the manuscript.

```{r results-paragraph, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results='asis'}

cat(para, "\n")

if (!docx_written) {
  cat("\n\n*(Word export skipped: install the officer package, or render from",
      "RStudio so that pandoc is on the path. The text above was still written",
      "to a .md file alongside this document.)*\n")
}

```
